units.title: The actual second-order entropy integral for bounded perturbations
units.classification: canonical finite-measure analytic prerequisite; not a complete textbook exercise
units.statement: Let mu be a finite measure on any measurable space, and let f be real-valued, a.e. strongly measurable and uniformly a.e. bounded by some finite real M. The compensated entropy integral of 1+epsilon*f, divided by epsilon squared, tends as nonzero real epsilon tends to zero to one half of the integral of f squared. No centering, probability normalization, differentiability of f or supplied convergence certificate is needed for this compensated statement.
assumptions: The measure mu is finite. It need not be a probability law, nonzero, sigma-finite by a separate premise, or defined by a smooth Gibbs density.

The real function f is a.e. strongly measurable and |f| <= M almost everywhere for one finite real M. No pointwise representative, smoothness or compact support is required. The proof uses |M|, so no extra M>=0 premise or division by M is introduced.

The parameter limit is the two-sided punctured real neighborhood of zero. The totalized quotient value at epsilon=0 is irrelevant. The logarithm arguments are proved positive eventually almost everywhere.

steps.title: Compensate the first-order term
steps.text: Use Mathlib's existing klFun rather than defining another entropy. Substitution cancels the constant term. Centering is unnecessary at this stage: subtracting epsilon*f is part of the integrand, not a theorem hypothesis.
steps.lean: The statement uses InformationTheory.klFun. Its literal definition is x*log(x)+1-x.

steps.title: Prove the scalar coefficient using genuine derivatives
steps.text: For a fixed real a, the logarithm is genuinely differentiable near epsilon=0 because its argument is near 1, not 0. Its slope quotient tends to a. Differentiate the compensated numerator and epsilon squared, then apply punctured two-sided L'Hopital. This includes a=0 without dividing by a.
steps.lean: The private scalar_limit uses hasDerivAt_klFun, Real.hasDerivAt_log, HasDerivAt.tendsto_slope_zero and HasDerivAt.lhopital_zero_nhdsNE. No conclusion is read from a totalized derivative at zero.

steps.title: Construct the quadratic envelope
steps.text: For u>=0, convexity gives q(u)>=0. The elementary log inequality log(u)<=u-1 gives q(u)<=(u-1)^2 for u>0; handle u=0 separately. Boundedness makes |epsilon|*|M|<1 eventually and hence 1+epsilon*f>0 almost everywhere. Divide the envelope by epsilon squared only for nonzero epsilon.
steps.lean: klFun_nonneg and the private klFun_upper produce the bounds. The eventually-small parameter and the a.e. bound are combined explicitly; mul_div_cancel_left0 cancels the nonzero square.

steps.title: Discharge measurability and integrability
steps.text: Finite measure and the essential bound imply that f squared is integrable. Continuity of klFun and the measurable arithmetic operations make every parameter integrand a.e. strongly measurable. These are produced inside the proof rather than assumed as certificates.
steps.lean: Integrable.mono' starts from integrable_const. continuous_klFun.comp_aestronglyMeasurable constructs the parameter integrands.

steps.title: Pass the actual limit through the integral
steps.text: Apply filter dominated convergence with the single integrable dominator f squared. The pointwise limit is the scalar result, and the bounds hold eventually almost everywhere. Pull the parameter-dependent scalar outside each Bochner integral to obtain exactly the displayed quotient limit.

steps.title: Keep the source consumers separate
steps.text: For a probability law and centered f, the later adapter must prove that the actual positive density has mass one, identify its Radon-Nikodym derivative and finite canonical KL, and remove the compensated linear term. The LSI application, Fisher limit and exact PI test domain require their own proofs. Centering a compact function generally leaves the function noncompact, although its gradient remains compactly supported.
steps.lean: These are downstream obligations, not conclusions of this declaration or new public assumptions on a complete Exercise 1.7 theorem.

units.lean_statement: The exact statement quantifies over any measurable carrier and finite measure, with one a.e. bound. It concerns the compensated klFun integral, not canonical klDiv of probability laws.
units.lean_proof: A scalar genuine-derivative limit plus a uniform quadratic envelope feed a fully discharged filter dominated-convergence argument. Private helpers share the public result's whole-module review and earn no separate leaf credit.
